sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Channel Omni-Helpdesk and Conversational Bot Cloud

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 31 August 1994, in force 1 January 1996, as amended)
France–China Agreement on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (signed 1984)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (signed 19 June 2008)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied to France)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 to R.561-42; Article L.561-2-2 (definition of beneficial owner); Articles L.561-45 to L.561-48 (UBO declaration and register); French Commercial Code, Articles L.123-1 to L.123-18 and R.123-10-1 to R.123-219 (RCS and UBO filing); Décret n°2020-118 of 12 February 2020, as amended; transposition of Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the beneficial owner's valid national passport (biometric data page only)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing government authority in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French consular legalisation where Apostille is not available

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and memorandum/articles of association of any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or official corporate existence certificate for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Company Register or tax authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent proof of residential address of each individual UBO (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalisation or sworn certified French translation; Apostille not required for domestic French documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, and UBOs must be screened against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions database (EEAS/FSD), the French national asset-freeze register (DGT/Assanet), and the OFAC SDN List due to the use of USD-denominated payment rails (Stripe Billing and PayPal). PEP status is captured through commercial PEP databases and self-disclosure; any PEP or PEP-related UBO automatically triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and potential TRACFIN reportability under Article L.561-15 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. The Low_Risk_Standard classification of the helpdesk/SaaS activity does not derogate from these mandatory AML/CFT controls.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.inpi.fr) and Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) search via data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate filings in the RCS must be submitted in French using Latin script. A proposed corporate name containing non-French terms or non-Latin lettering is transliterated into the French roman alphabet before registration. There is no absolute prohibition on foreign-language names, provided the name is not contrary to public order or good morals, is not likely to mislead the public, and is distinguishable from names already recorded in the RNCS database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal statutory name-reservation window for French sociétés. An INPI/RNCS availability check should be treated as valid for 30 days; a fresh search must be run immediately before final filing. If the Guichet unique/INPI rejects the proposed name, the applicant may re-file with an amended name without penalty. Where the rejection is based on an asserted third-party trademark or a resemblance conflict, the applicant may submit a written request for human review to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce. A formal refusal can be contested by petition to the President of the Tribunal Judiciaire (or Tribunal de Commerce in respect of commercial conflicts) under summary procedure, within 15 days of notification, and interim injunctive relief is available in urgent cases.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an SAS only through a licensed domiciliation agent under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code. The domiciliation agent must not be the statutory auditor or a corporate officer of the company. The contractual address must be effective and verifiable in the RCS. For a low-risk helpdesk/SaaS activity, a virtual office arrangement is commercially acceptable, provided substantive management, accounting, tax compliance, and board decision-making remain effectively exercised in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5.0% estimated annual probability; unannounced on-site inspections are uncommon for non-regulated low-risk helpdesk/SaaS enterprises, but may occur where the domiciliation agent is flagged by the Greffe/DGFiP or where UBO or payment-rail indicators trigger enhanced review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official corporate formation filing fee via the INPI Guichet unique (including digital filing and submission of UBO declaration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff applicable to the Guichet unique national formalities service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) registration tariff for a SAS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce competent for the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff annexed to the applicable French commercial registry fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Compulsory legal announcement of incorporation in a journal of legal notices (journal d'annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SAS incorporation announcement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation agreement with a licensed domiciliation agent (first full year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation agent regulated under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SAS domiciliation contract in a major French city

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, consular legalisation, and certified French translation of foreign UBO/KYC documentation (package for two foreign individual UBOs or corporate shareholders)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notarial or consular authorities in origin countries and certified legal translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial and certified-translation market rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel fixed fee for drafting SAS articles of association (statuts), UBO declaration, and filing coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French licensed counsel or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for a single-shareholder SAS with standard object and no notarial capital contribution

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company law) and L.227-1 to L.227-10 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Décret n° 2021-1803 du 23 décembre 2021 on the Guichet Unique formalities; relevant articles of the Code de l'environnement for non-industrial service activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with substantive legal registration by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office jurisdiction (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de Constitution de Société (electronic M0 declaration) filed via the official portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; the registry subsequently issues the official Extrait Kbis as proof of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS under Article L.224-2 of the French Commercial Code. However, the full subscribed capital must be paid up at incorporation; cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked capital account opened at a bank, notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and the funds are released only upon issuance of the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the Sole Shareholder of the SAS, pursuant to Articles L.224-2, L.227-1 and L.227-9 of the French Commercial Code, that: (1) the entire share capital of EUR 1,000, divided into 1,000 ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 each, is hereby subscribed and fully paid, the funds having been deposited in a blocked capital account in accordance with law; (2) the registered office is fixed at [Address], Paris, France, and the President is authorised to complete all formalities; (3) [Name] is appointed Président with full powers to represent the Company, and [Name] is appointed statutory auditor for a six-year mandate; (4) the Kbis filing, legal publication and all ancillary governance acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital and Opening of a Blocked Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised credit institution in France, a notaire public, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account in the name of the company in formation; transfer the full cash portion of the subscribed share capital; obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds / attestation de blocage certifying that the funds are held and blocked; the certificate must be addressed to the persons empowered to sign the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (projet de statuts)
Identity documents of all subscribing shareholders
Power of attorney (mandat) for any representative
Optional company name reservation certificate (certificat de réservation de nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the blocking certificate because of a capital shortfall, the shareholders must immediately wire the missing amount; if the proposed company name is unavailable, reserve an alternative name with the INPI and re-file the banking instructions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The shareholders themselves; a notaire public may be used but is not mandatory for an SAS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholders must sign the final statuts, either in original paper form or by secure electronic signature under Articles 1367-1 and 1367-2 of the French Civil Code. The statuts must state the legal form (SAS), corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose aligned with ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 (helpdesk and conversational bot cloud services), share capital, share distribution, and the appointment of the Président.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (statuts)
Blocked funds certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Identity and address proof of each shareholder
Certificate of non-residence or tax residence statement where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a signature is defective or a shareholder refuses to sign, the constitutional act must be regularised by a rectification deed (acte rectificatif) or by convening a new shareholder signature session; the existing blocked funds certificate remains valid if the capital structure is unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Notice (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) in the department where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a French-language incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form (SAS), registered office, corporate object, share capital, and special provisions; publish the notice in the JAL and obtain the attestation de parution; this attestation is mandatory for the subsequent Guichet Unique filing.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association
Blocked capital certificate
Power of attorney to the JAL publisher
Draft publication text
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice due to drafting defects, correct the wording and republish; the incorporation registration deadline is automatically extended for up to 15 days upon proof of new publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Declaration on Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the INPI, with internal transmission to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an account on the Guichet Unique portal; complete the standard M0 form (déclaration de société commerciale); answer the prescreening questionnaire; upload all mandatory attachments; pay the statutory fee of EUR 49.90 electronically; submit the file and retain the time-stamped acknowledgement of receipt; the INPI then routes the file to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 electronic declaration
Signed Articles of Association executed by all shareholders
Attestation de dépôt des blocage des fonds for cash shares
Attestation de parution issued by the JAL
Justificatif de jouissance des locaux (right to use the registered office premise)
Copy of the President's identity document and sworn declaration of no criminal record
Proof of payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a réquisition (request for completion), respond in writing within 15 days, amend or complete the documents in the online portal, and resubmit; failure to cure leads to rejection, but a fresh application may be re-filed with corrected data without loss of the original company name reservation if still valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of the Extrait Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (e.g., Greffe de Paris) under the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and INSEE for SIREN/SIRET allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies formal legal completeness and registers the SAS in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; INSEE assigns the SIREN and SIRET numbers; the registry issues the official Extrait Kbis (incorporation certificate); upon receipt of the Kbis, the company may open its definitive bank account and release the blocked capital to the statutory representative.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique filing acknowledgement
Transmitted registration file (M0 and attachments)
Proof of final registry fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RNE/Kbis registration contains errors or is refused, follow the Greffe's rectification procedure by filing a formal request (requête en rectification) or appeal the refusal before the president of the commercial court within one month of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable. The ISIC 6201 helpdesk and conversational bot cloud service is a non-manufacturing office activity and falls outside the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) nomenclature under the Code de l'environnement; therefore no industrial development or operating license is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no sectoral industrial or operational permit is triggered for the declared activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), under the Ministère de la Transition Écologique
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is not listed under the Annex I or Annex II case-by-case screening categories of Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code, and no ICPE registration or authorization is required for pure office/software services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Non-manufacturing office use: wastewater discharge must comply with municipal sewerage by-laws under Article L.1331-1 et seq. of the Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales; VOC emissions are de minimis from office cleaning and printing operations; IT hardware disposal must comply with WEEE extended producer responsibility rules; no industrial effluent or atmospheric emission thresholds are applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: for premises receiving the public (ERP), a fire safety declaration to the Commission de Sécurité (Préfecture de Police) and periodic visits apply; for pure office premises a simple structural and fire-safety conformity statement under Code du travail Articles R.4227-1 et seq. is required. Structural load clearance is recommended for server and telecom rooms. Occupational health: registration with the occupational health service (Service de Prévention et de Santé au Travail / CARSAT) and compliance with Code du travail Articles L.4121-1 and R.4222-1 on ventilation and workplace safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). The principal online tax portal is impots.gouv.fr; business-formation formalities are filed through the INPI-operated Guichet unique.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SAS through the Guichet unique before commencing business. The formalities are transmitted to the competent registries and tax authorities; the company receives a SIREN and establishment-level SIRET. The SIE assigns or confirms the French VAT identification number, generally comprising FR, a two-digit control key, and the nine-digit SIREN. The company should activate its professional account on impots.gouv.fr and request VAT registration or confirmation from the SIE if the VAT number is not issued automatically or taxable transactions require it. Non-established foreign businesses making taxable supplies in France generally apply to the designated non-resident tax service and may need a French fiscal representative if established outside the EU/EEA and outside a qualifying mutual-assistance arrangement. EU-established businesses generally do not require a French fiscal representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). An eligible qualifying SAS may elect temporary income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, IR), generally for no more than five fiscal years and subject to statutory ownership, activity, size, age, and consent conditions. This is not a US-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement applicable EU and OECD measures; no general election permits a SAS to choose a transparent classification for cross-border purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a France-established business, the domestic VAT exemption for small businesses (franchise en base) generally applies to services only while prior-year turnover does not exceed EUR 37,500, subject to a EUR 41,250 current-year tolerance threshold; exceeding the applicable threshold ends the exemption under the statutory rules. These thresholds do not operate as a general registration safe harbor for foreign businesses, and other special rules may apply. A French SAS making taxable domestic supplies must register once liable to account for VAT. For SaaS and helpdesk services, place-of-supply rules are material: qualifying B2B supplies are generally taxed where the business customer is established, often with customer-accounted reverse charge; B2C electronically supplied services are generally taxed where the consumer is located, with EU cross-border B2C VAT potentially reportable through the Union OSS. The EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold is a limited place-of-supply rule for qualifying EU-established suppliers, not a general French VAT-registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not generally require real-time tax-authority clearance or fiscal stamping of invoices. Domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction/payment e-reporting are being phased in through approved or registered platforms under the French reform: all in-scope businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance and reporting obligations begin 1 September 2026 for large and intermediate-sized enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises, subject to statutory scope and any implementing changes. The platform transmits required invoice data to the tax administration. Cross-border and B2C transactions are generally subject to e-reporting rather than the domestic B2B e-invoicing requirement where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the EU may be exempt with a right to deduct input VAT when the statutory export conditions are met and the supplier can substantiate that the goods left the EU. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State and the supplier holds prescribed evidence and reporting support. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: B2B services are generally located where the customer is established under the general rule, while B2C electronically supplied services are generally taxed where the consumer is located; specific statutory exceptions apply. A French supplier should retain evidence of customer status, contractual scope, place of supply, payment, and any required VAT-number and reporting checks.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and evidence of exit from the EU customs territory, such as the electronic exit confirmation or equivalent customs-certified proof
Commercial invoice, customer order or contract, and transport evidence such as a bill of lading, air waybill, or carrier delivery record, as relevant
Evidence supporting the customer's location and status and the applicable place-of-supply treatment for services, including VAT identification verification where relevant
An inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory prerequisite for export VAT exemption; retain payment and foreign-exchange records where relevant to substantiate the transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated to France. Incorrectly exempted or zero-rated supplies may result in assessment of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties. The standard tax penalty for an intentional breach is generally 40%; fraudulent conduct may attract a 80% penalty, subject to the facts and statutory conditions. False documentation, concealed transactions, or other serious conduct may also trigger separate civil or criminal consequences. Input VAT deductions or refunds may be denied or recovered retrospectively where export evidence, customer status, place of supply, or required declarations cannot be substantiated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) for monetary, statistical and balance-of-payments reporting functions, acting within the Eurosystem; the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty for external financial relations and foreign investment screening; the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for prudential supervision of banks and payment institutions engaged in onboarding, KYC and AML controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. France applies complete current-account and capital-account convertibility pursuant to Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Articles L152-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code. No prior exchange-control licence, foreign-exchange approval or central-bank clearance is required for capital contributions, profit remittance, dividend distributions, or payments for exported electronic services. Profit-remittance friction is exclusively fiscal: distributions by an SAS to non-resident corporate shareholders normally bear French withholding tax at 25%, reducible under an applicable double-tax treaty (e.g., 0-15% under the France-US treaty) or fully exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the EU-resident corporate shareholder satisfies the holding period and participation thresholds; source-country exchange-control approval does not exist for euro-denominated flows. Soft compliance frictions derive from the ACPR/FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists and EU Regulation 2020/1155 sanctions screening, which may delay execution but do not impair legal convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil. No statutory surrender ratio, repatriation deadline or mandatory conversion rule applies to French export receipts. Exchange controls were fully liberalised effective 1 January 1990 (Law No. 88-1149 of 23 December 1988) and the freedom principle is codified in Article L152-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code; SaaS subscription receipts may be collected in EUR or foreign currency and retained indefinitely. Residual obligations: (i) statistical Balance-of-Payments reporting to the Banque de France through the servicing credit institution for each cross-border wire transfer meeting the individual declaration threshold currently applicable; (ii) declaration of cross-border physical cash and bearer instruments above EUR 10,000 under EU Regulation 2018/1672; (iii) maintenance of complete electronic-service invoicing to evidence the export transaction for VAT and transfer-pricing purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (blocked consignation account for statutory capital deposit prior to RCS registration)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability as complementary collection and disbursement layer; Medium viability as sole treasury hub. ACPR-licensed French payment or electronic-money institutions (Qonto, Shine, Mangopay, Stripe France) may lawfully deliver SEPA IBANs, payment accounts and FX conversion services without a full banking licence; legal constraint is that payment-account funds are guaranteed by the partner credit institution within the EUR 100,000 FGDR cap and such EMIs cannot provide Banque de France refinancing, commercial letters of credit, or classical credit facilities. Cross-border EMIs (Wise via Belgian licence, Revolut via Lithuanian prudential passporting) may operate in France under PSD2 passporting but should be restricted to FX-optimised payouts for contractors and ad-hoc disbursements. Stripe Billing and PayPal remain the contractual inbound subscription rails for this Low_Risk_Standard profile, settling in EUR to the primary French operational account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law and ACPR guidelines do not impose an absolute physical-attendance mandate; remote onboarding is lawful where the bank applies an ANSSI-certified electronic identification scheme (France Identité, eIDAS Qualified Electronic Signature) or an ACPR-recognised third-party video-verification process. In practice, tier-1 universal banks (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole/LCL) require at least one in-branch or hybrid attend by the SAS president and any natural-person UBO controlling 25% or more, with the corporate UBO chain evidenced by notarised registry extracts and apostilled translations. Fully remote first signature is reliably available only at fintech EMIs and digital banks (Qonto, Shine, Boursorama Pro). A prudent treasury policy mandates that only the French-resident president executes the banking mandate, avoiding reliance on a foreign-resident officer for the KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate UBO opacity: a non-resident parent or an intermediate holding company owns over 25% of the SAS and the natural-person ultimate beneficiary is not transparent from the initial KYB screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Infogreffe extract Kbis of the SAS; statutory Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO declaration); translated and apostilled corporate registry extracts of the parent and any intermediate holding entities; certified passport copies of every natural person exercising direct or indirect control of 25% or more; the SAS statuts; delegation-of-authority matrix of the president's powers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Letterbox-company flag: newly formed French SAS with low headcount collecting SaaS revenue through overseas processors, prompting the bank to question economic substance and the residency of management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease (bail commercial) for the registered head office; French payroll social declarations (DSN) for local staff; French VAT and corporate income tax filings; minutes of shareholders' and board meetings held in France; client support SLAs evidencing active service delivery; first-period financial statements or certified accountant attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds challenge on the inbound capital injection: non-resident parent wires share capital, triggering suspicion of undisclosed intra-group financing, money remittance or loan-stacking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Parent board resolution authorising the capital increase or contribution; SWIFT MT103/202 trail showing the euros credited from the parent's high-rated bank; the parent's audited financial statements for the last two years; source-of-funds declaration describing the treasury provenance; bank attestation de dépôt de fonds for the SAS capital; minutes of the extraordinary general meeting approving the capital increase.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEPs screening ambiguity: UBO or president surname produces false-positive hits against EU/OFAEC lists, or the SAS's client geo-history includes high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: QES-signed KYC questionnaire with full legal name, date of birth and place of birth for disambiguation; notarised birth certificate and identity document; Stripe/PayPal settlement reports proving EU-centric subscriber base; list of countries restricted by the company's sanctions compliance policy; OECD tax-residency certificate demonstrating non-exposure to Article 238-0 A states; legal letter confirming the commercial purpose of transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction classification: shareholder or ultimate parent incorporated in a jurisdiction listed by FATF/ACPR or by France's non-cooperative-state list under Article 238-0 A of the French General Tax Code, blocking standard KYC sign-off.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and sworn-translated corporate charter and registry certificate from the foreign jurisdiction; economic-substance report of the parent (local management, premises, payroll, turnover); evidence of the applicable EU withholding or treaty regime; transfer-pricing documentation (Master File/Local File if thresholds are met); correspondence from the foreign tax authority evidencing exchange-of-information cooperation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) the non-resident parent board passes a written resolution approving the SAS capital increase; (ii) funds are transmitted by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA SCT in EUR) to the SAS's EUR IBAN citing ISO 20022 ExternalPurposeCode 'INVE' with remittance narrative 'French SAS share capital contribution / apport en numéraire'; (iii) the receiving French bank files the individual Balance-of-Payments statistical report to the Banque de France, classifying the flow as direct investment - equity capital under BPM6; (iv) the funds are deposited in a blocked escrow account or accepted by the bank/notary with an attestation de dépôt de fonds, then released upon issuance of the RCS registration; (v) no ex-ante authorisation from the Direction Générale du Trésor is required because an ISIC 6201 helpdesk/SaaS business is outside the sensitive sectors listed in Article R151-3 of the Monetary and Financial Code, unless the product includes cybersecurity or security-operations functionality; (vi) the SAS registers the UBO declaration and any capital-modification formality with the commercial registry within the legal filing window.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails aligned to an ISIC 6201 service exporter: (i) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for EUR settlements to French/EU suppliers, contractors and commission agents; (ii) SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking for non-EU and foreign-currency counterparties (US cloud infrastructure, sub-agents, overseas IBAN payees) using ISO 20022 purpose codes such as 'SUPP' (supplier settlement), 'ROYA' (royalty/licence fees) and 'DIVI' (dividend distribution), with the French bank performing the balance-of-payments classification; (iii) commercial letters of credit are unnecessary for electronic-service exports and should be refused as non-cost-effective; the operative documentary toolkit is the VAT-compliant invoice, proof of service delivery and e-contract; (iv) subscription proceeds from Stripe Billing and PayPal settle in EUR to the primary operational account under the processors' standard settlement calendars, after which treasury sweeps redistribute liquidity to the disbursement account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot (change au comptant) for the conversion of USD/GBP balances accumulated from multi-currency Stripe and PayPal settlements, executed through the treasury bank or the fintech EMI's FX desk without derivative documentation.

Outright FX forwards (change à terme) with maturities up to 12 months, documented under an ISDA/FBF master agreement with the French treasury bank, executed only to hedge a committed and verifiable invoice pipeline and classified as fair-value hedges under Article L211-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code.

European plain-vanilla FX options and zero-premium option combinations for hedging uncertain cross-border subscription revenue, subject to prior board resolution, credit-relationship approval and mandatory EMIR reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the EUR is the settlement leg, permitted only for currencies lacking deliverable onshore forward markets (e.g., certain African and emerging-market currencies) and executed through an ACPR-licensed counterparty to preserve French balance-of-payments transparency.

Cross-currency interest rate and principal swaps (XCCY/CIRS) reserved for long-term non-EUR debt or locked-in foreign-currency revenue exceeding EUR 5 million annually, requiring a legal entity identifier (LEI), EMIR margining and trade-repository reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Assemblée Générale Ordinaire, AGO — annual shareholder meeting approving the French statutory accounts, profit appropriation and resolutions; minutes recorded in the official minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed directly; the signed AGM minutes (procès-verbal) are attached to the annual accounts deposit at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the RCS dossier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year (one-off court extension available)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-convening permits any shareholder or the Public Prosecutor to petition the commercial court to appoint a mandataire to call the meeting; the related 7-month statutory accounts-filing deadline is missed and the RCS dossier becomes irregular

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Comptes annuels — annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes) plus management report, by the Président, and Statutory Auditor's report if one is appointed; deposited at the French Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the France Greffe / Infogreffe electronic filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of AGM approval and in any event within 7 months after the financial year close; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing deposit triggers a court-ordered daily penalty (astreinte) at the request of any interested party, criminal fines for the Président/legal entity, loss of investor/credit credibility, and persistent default exposes the SAS to judicial strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs — annual beneficial-owner register confirmation identifying each natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 25% or exercising sufficient control over the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) — filed simultaneously with the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Comptes annuels deposit (by 31 July for a calendar-year entity); any ownership change exceeding the UBO threshold must be re-filed within 30 days of the relevant share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal sanctions under Article L.574-5 of the Code Monétaire et Financier: up to 6 months' imprisonment and a €7,500 fine for natural persons, €37,500 fine for the legal entity, in addition to being treated as non-compliant for all RCS formalities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Liasse fiscale — annual corporation tax return comprising Form 2065 and 2031/2050 schedules: taxable result, balance-sheet annexes, depreciation, provisions, and profit-distribution details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — mandatory online filing (télédéclaration) through the professional EDI/EFI business portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of the financial year close; for a 31 December year-end, by 3 May of the following year via e-filing, with the final tax balance (solde d'IS) payable by 15 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax, rising to 40% where no return is filed after a formal notice (mise en demeure), plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; fixed fines apply to omitted annexes even in loss-making years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) — annual local business levy with the municipal minimum contribution, payable by any SAS carrying on a business in France on 1 January of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP local tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) of the registered business premises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 15 December of the current tax year (tax notice issued in November); a SAS created during the year is exempt from CFE for its first year of activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-payment results in an immediate 10% penalty plus monthly interest of 0.20%, enforced by garnishment orders, and the enterprise can no longer claim cancellation remedies for the year concerned

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Commissaire aux Comptes is mandatory where the SAS exceeds two of three thresholds: total balance sheet greater than €4,000,000; net turnover greater than €8,000,000; and an average workforce greater than 50 employees. A small helpdesk SaaS entity below these thresholds has no statutory audit; audit appointment remains possible voluntarily for shareholders collectively holding at least 10% of share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be drawn up under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général / Règlement ANC n°2014-03, as amended); IFRS is permitted only for consolidated accounts of groups whose securities are listed on a regulated market.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must maintain the RCS beneficial-owner file current at all times: any share transfer that creates or modifies a qualifying UBO interest (>25% ownership, voting power or controlling executive power) must be declared to the Greffe within 30 days, and a fresh UBO declaration accompanies every annual accounts filing even when no ownership change has occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (register of share transfers and ownership movements)
Registre des décisions des associés / procès-verbaux d'assemblée (shareholders' decision and minute book)
Registre des décisions du président (minute book recording the Président's decisions taken under the SAS articles)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% standard rate; 15% preferential rate for SMEs with turnover ≤ €50 million; R&D, innovation and other tax credits/deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200 - Déclaration de résultat de l'exercice via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (15th day of the 4th month following year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover including sales and services revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for French tax-resident entities; non-residents report only French-source income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French tax base adjustments and deductions applied

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax calculation after deductions and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply reduced rates or incentives where eligible

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% of tax due per month of delay (minimum €50), capped at 25% of tax due; criminal prosecution possible for evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Titre de Résidence Certifié (TRC) from French tax authorities and submit with withholding declaration via impots.gouv.fr to claim reduced treaty rates
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 12.8% statutory (0-10% under most treaties); Interest: 0% generally for related-party debt (reduced by treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Limited applicability under French law; general GAAR and substance requirements apply to maintain tax residency

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late or non-filing of corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit Form 1200 by statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty 0.75% per month of delay on tax due (max 25%); possible criminal imprisonment for willful evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unpaid taxes; potential disqualification, restitution orders and criminal sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of TP documentation or use of non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest and penalties up to 80% of additional tax due
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal liability for fraudulent declarations; possible imprisonment and personal restitution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Understatement of taxable income or false documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Hiding revenue, issuing fake invoices or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 80% of evaded tax; criminal imprisonment up to 5 years and confiscation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal civil and criminal liability; possible travel bans, fines and disqualification from office
